brief: brief-js166-time.md. The owner: dogfood-specific sizing is not necessarily indicative of the typical user and may not be the best use of time. D-064's sizing correction is live (the 12-thread worker's CPU limit 8 to 12, request 500m to 6, declared transcodeCores 3.5 to 3.2). Before it, 4 of 16 parts missed JS-166 criterion 3's bound, all on one 4K HDR film, three of them burned-in (playback 0.963 to 0.992 after 30 s, 4 to 25 freezes, longest 2.0 s). After it, with the stored segments deleted, the plain start (1.36x encode) and one burned-in start (1.285x) played at 1.000 with no freeze and no segment request over 5 s, one run each. The second burned-in start and the seek were not re-measured. An earlier replay was invalid because it served stored segments. Options: A finish the remaining parts (about 45 minutes of browser runs, JS-041 waits); B close with the evidence at hand; C stop all dogfood sizing work and leave the docs; D as B but raise the declared figure to 3.4 to 3.6 first.
tradeoff: Given up: the proof, after the sizing correction, that a seek and a second burned-in start of a 4K HDR re-encode meet JS-166 criterion 3's bound on the dogfood, and three plays of each part and the play beside a subtitle extraction after the correction. Given up by the dogfood's operator and household: a stall in those parts, if one remains, is found by use and not by a staged run. The 12-thread worker stays declared at 3.2, below the 3.4 to 3.6 two runs imply, until JS-177 removes the figure; by the documented prices that admits the same plays (reasoned, not run). No viewer or operator of any other deployment loses anything.
entry: JS-166 closes as done on the evidence at hand; its record names what was not re-measured, and nothing unmeasured is written as passing. docs/status.md's 4K gap line is narrowed, not closed: the dogfood holds one such play at a time and refuses a second with its reason, with the two measured parts and the two unmeasured named. docs/transcoding.md gains the worker's row at limit 8 and limit 12 as one cluster's figures, one run each, not sizing guidance. No further sizing change is made to the dogfood until JS-177 merges and its declared figures are dropped. D-064's reopen condition on the replay is retired: it was not triggered by the two parts measured, and JS-041 starts now with JS-177 directly after it, so the reorder it guarded no longer exists. JS-174 loses its fallback of being taken on the dogfood under JS-166. BL-261 holds the unmeasured parts. Rejected: A (45 minutes of certainty for one cluster while a capability every household lacks waits, on no data that the play still fails); C (leaves the gap line and the measured row unwritten); D (a rollout for a figure that admits nothing more, rests on two runs and is deleted by JS-177). Unverified when decided: whether criteria 4, 5 and 8 of JS-166 were taken (each not taken is recorded so and comes to triage); the 3.4 to 3.6; that 3.2 and 3.6 admit the same plays; the worker's speed while its neighbours use the 4.85 threads they request. Reopens on: a 4K re-encode on the dogfood under 1.0x past its first 30 seconds, a slow-job reason counted there, or a household report of a stall (BL-261: one replay of that part, as a brief); a second deployment reporting a worker throttled under a CPU limit, which moves the 'Sizing workers' doc of JS-177 criterion 7 ahead as a docs-only change.
serves: Owner, 2026-11-22: 'Work that makes an existing capability more certain does not keep going ahead of a missing capability viewers would feel more, unless measured data shows that capability failing viewers now.' PRODUCT.md: 'Their languages come first' (JS-041), and 'Where a capability can't yet serve every film, the gap is written down and planned, not left as a quirk.'
